findings.description: The one word doing the real work in SHEET-FORMULA-004 — "stacked" — is never elaborated, and this is exactly where the two directions meet. The real code resolves "stacked" as two co-located, separately-headered, distinctly-typed bands published under the Tax surface: an accrual band (TAX_HEADER = Sale ID, Lot ID, Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Amount, Lifecycle State), one row per input Accrual, and a reserve-summary band (TAX_RESERVE_HEADER = Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Accrued, Moved, Paid, Outstanding, Shortfall), one row per (Jurisdiction, Tax Year) AnnualRow — pinned by tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows and reserve_summary_carries_all_five_kernel_exact_columns, with row-count parity (tax.accruals.rows.len()==accruals.len(); tax.reserve_summary.rows.len()==annual_rows.len()) and an explicit ban on either band's rows matching the other band's header verbatim. All three A-direction runs, working from the spec text alone, guessed three mutually incompatible and all-wrong meanings: A1 = one row per tax lot grouped by symbol with an invented TaxTerm field; A2 = a single cumulative per-symbol aggregate (KernelTaxFigure) carrying a SyncId; A3 = per-lot rows grouped and subtotaled by tax term into a TaxStack with per-term subtotals. None reconstructs the real accrual/reserve-summary split. Meanwhile all three B-direction runs independently and near-verbatim reconstruct the real two-band structure, headers, and row-count invariants from the code alone — proving the ambiguity is real (A can't guess it) and that the code is where all the load-bearing structure actually lives (B recovers it cleanly).

All three A-outputs add an explicit, carried "as of last sync" marker to the Tax figures, tracing directly to the spec's explicit "as-of-last-sync" phrase: A1 embeds an RFC3339 timestamp into a header row ("Tax — kernel-exact, as of {as_of}"); A2 attaches a per-figure SyncId plus a literal source_label "kernel (as of last sync)"; A3 attaches a per-row as_of_sync: DateTime<Utc> sourced from snapshot.as_of_sync. The real Tax tab has no such field anywhere — neither TAX_HEADER nor TAX_RESERVE_HEADER contains an as-of/sync/timestamp column, and TaxView/ViewTab carry no such metadata at all (contrast with Positions, which does stamp per-row freshness via its live GOOGLEFINANCE-driven "Quote Date" formula column). Freshness for the Tax tab is entirely implicit, governed elsewhere by Publisher's stale-tab/republish bookkeeping, not rendered into the tab's data. The spec's own wording ("as-of-last-sync") pushes every independent implementation toward a visible marker that the real Tax tab simply doesn't have.

The code and tests pin an enormous amount of exact, load-bearing detail that the one-sentence EARS text never states, and that none of the A-runs guessed: the precise currency-formatting algorithm fmt_cents ("{sign}{whole}.{frac:02}", sign only when negative, unsigned-abs split into whole/hundredths, two-zero-padded fraction, no '+' for non-negative) pinned by literal string assertions ("50.00", "-1.50"); the Jurisdiction label format "Federal" / "State(<code>)"; the fixed four-member Lifecycle State vocabulary "Accrued"/"Allocated"/"Moved"/"Paid" that discards any variant payload (e.g. Moved{..} collapses to "Moved"); the rule that an accrual with applied_cents == None renders Amount as an empty string (never "0.00", never an error placeholder); and the anti-corruption invariants that no accrual-band row may equal TAX_RESERVE_HEADER verbatim and every row's width must equal its own band's header width. None of this is derivable from SHEET-FORMULA-004's text, yet B1/B2/B3 reconstruct it almost identically (high cross-run agreement) — the terse spec is silent on essentially all of the concrete, test-enforced behavior that actually exists.

Minor/weak: only A1 invents an empty-tax-lots fallback (a placeholder text row "No tax lots as of last sync") rather than an empty tab; A2 and A3 instead correctly default to an empty Vec on empty input, matching the real code's actual behavior (zero accruals -> zero rows, no placeholder). Since this isn't unanimous across A-runs and doesn't trace to explicit spec text, it reads as a one-off assumption artifact rather than a hard finding, but it does contribute to the low cross-run agreement on Direction A.

notes: Real code: sheets-view's render_tax() (lib.rs lines 707-750) produces a TaxView { accruals: ViewTab under TAX_HEADER, reserve_summary: ViewTab under TAX_RESERVE_HEADER }. TAX_HEADER = [Sale ID, Lot ID, Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Amount, Lifecycle State]; TAX_RESERVE_HEADER = [Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Accrued, Moved, Paid, Outstanding, Shortfall]. Every cell is Cell::Value (never Cell::Formula) in both bands, pinned by tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula in formula.rs. Formatting: fmt_cents (sign+whole.frac two-digit), jurisdiction_label (\"Federal\"/\"State(code)\"), lifecycle_label (Accrued/Allocated/Moved/Paid). Amount is a.applied_cents.map(fmt_cents).unwrap_or_default() (empty string when None). Row-count and anti-corruption invariants tested in tabs.rs (publishes_four_view_tabs_one_row_per_entity, tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows) and formula.rs (reserve_summary_carries_all_five_kernel_exact_columns). None of the A-direction sketches (built from the terse EARS text alone) reconstruct this two-band schema; all three B-direction reconstructions (built from the code alone) recover it with high fidelity, including exact header lists, formatting rules, and row-count invariants — differing mainly in EARS-categorization style and whether they quote the literal tab-name strings (only B3 quotes \"Tax\" / \"Tax · Reserve Summary\" verbatim, matching TAX_TAB/TAX_RESERVE_TAB constants exactly).
